recent_posts.title: Richard Geldreich's Blog: bug found in Intel's ASTC compressor (part of ispc
recent_posts.summary: A bug was discovered in Intel's ASTC texture compressor (ispc_texcomp) while porting it to pure C for benchmarking. The swap() utility function for float values contains a typo that incorrectly casts the first value to int, affecting floating point operations including block error scoring. The author plans to release the C port on GitHub after further testing with UBSan for undefined behavior and statistical analysis of ASTC output. The port has already been enhanced with sRGB decode support, candidate generation, and per-channel weights.

recent_posts.title: Richard Geldreich's Blog: Block blurring (prefiltering)
recent_posts.summary: GPU texture compressors can use prefiltering (blurring) as a technique to improve perceptual quality when an encoder overfits edges. By blurring the input before re-encoding the worst blocks (measured by SSIM), overall perceptual quality can paradoxically improve despite the blur.

recent_posts.title: Richard Geldreich's Blog: Petascale changes everything
recent_posts.summary: At petabyte scale, adding GPU texture support to apps with existing JPEG/WebP content presents three options: encoding to multiple uncompressed formats (impractical due to 8-16x size explosion), using supercompression to a universal format with on-device transcoding (adds ~1-1.5 PB, driver-independent, Khronos-standardized), or using compute shaders for transcoding (plagued by mobile GPU driver bugs, limited to smaller ASTC block sizes). Supercompression is argued as the only viable approach at scale, enabling larger ASTC block sizes (8x8, 10x10, 12x12) and eliminating driver-dependent failure modes that become intolerable when serving hundreds of millions to over a billion users.

recent_posts.title: Richard Geldreich's Blog: Large block size ASTC has been misunderstood
recent_posts.summary: Rich Geldreich argues that large block size ASTC (10x10, 12x12) has been widely misunderstood by game developers. These block sizes were designed for high-resolution (4K) content and offer dramatic memory bandwidth savings (0.89–1.28 bpp). GPU shader deblocking at these sizes is essentially free on mobile/tablet hardware where memory bandwidth is the bottleneck. He notes that existing encoders are incomplete or broken — Intel's ispc_texcomp lacked multi-subset support and is now archived, while ARM's LDR encoder lacks deblocking awareness and supercompression support. The path forward involves deblocking-aware encoders that exploit deblocking like modern image/video codecs have done for decades.

recent_posts.title: Richard Geldreich's Blog: XUASTC's next step: Intra-prediction of weight grids
recent_posts.summary: Rich Geldreich outlines the next development step for XUASTC, Binomial's GPU texture compression format. Currently, XUASTC applies JPEG-style DCT coding to ASTC weight grids, including standard luminance quantization tables with adaptive quantization. The proposed improvement is to port WebP-style intra-prediction into the weight grid domain — predicting weight grids from neighboring blocks and then coding only the residuals with DCT. This approach mirrors how modern image codecs work and is expected to push bitrates lower, especially at very low quality factors where pure DCT struggles. The author emphasizes targeting existing hardware decoders rather than neural compression techniques.

recent_posts.title: Richard Geldreich's Blog: .ASTC (the File Format): No Longer a Black Box
recent_posts.summary: The basisu command line tool has a new -peek option that opens standard ARM LDR/HDR .ASTC texture files, unpacks each block, and computes statistics about the ASTC configurations used. This tool revealed that Intel's ispc_texcomp ASTC encoder is effectively broken for practical use.

recent_posts.title: Richard Geldreich's Blog: ASTC Decoding: Software Decoders, Spec Issues, and ARM Errata
recent_posts.summary: A brief post pointing to a curated wiki page listing available software ASTC decoders, along with notes on spec issues and ARM errata related to ASTC decoding. The linked resource is hosted on the Basis Universal GitHub wiki.

recent_posts.title: Richard Geldreich's Blog: ARM ASTC Decoding Errata
recent_posts.summary: A brief post by Rich Geldreich pointing to ARM's official ASTC decoding errata document and a wiki listing available software ASTC decoders, highlighting real-world complexities in decoding the ASTC texture compression format.

recent_posts.title: Richard Geldreich's Blog: Some things we've learned
recent_posts.summary: Richard Geldreich shares six key lessons learned from Binomial's customers about GPU texture compression at scale. The main takeaways: bitrate is the top priority at petabyte scale, ASTC dominates with billions of devices while everything else is a fallback, GPU drivers are unreliable so compute shaders should be avoided, all 14 ASTC block sizes matter, WASM SIMD cannot be assumed, and all encoders/decoders must be fuzzed since no data can be trusted.

recent_posts.title: Richard Geldreich's Blog: The Three Eras of GPU Texture Distribution
recent_posts.summary: A brief pointer to the Basis Universal v2.0 wiki article titled 'The Three Eras of GPU Texture Distribution,' authored by Rich Geldreich. The linked wiki page covers the historical evolution of GPU texture distribution formats and technologies.
